_comment: Plane-4 standing tool-surface baseline (scripts/check-tool-surface.mjs). Growth is ALLOWED but never silent: raise a value and record `reason` + `recordedAt` saying what capability it buys. Dispatch-time caps are governed elsewhere and are not the subject of this baseline.

registry.toolDefinitions.reason: BI-012487AA (slice A4 of the integrated office suite roadmap) adds create_report, create_letter, create_sheet and create_drawing beside create_presentation in the existing document pack. spec.ts and renderDocument already produce all five families, but only decks (and EA views) had a coworker door, so a finance controller could not produce a board report, a budget workbook or a donor letter, and nobody could draw a free diagram. Four intent-named tools, not one create_document(family, spec): the outlines differ (sections, an addressed letter, tables with formulas, shapes and arrows), and one tool with five discriminated unions is the weakest selection surface; each tool is a profile plus an outline mapping over ONE shared pipeline (family-document.ts), which create_presentation now also runs on. Outside the core tier; reached through document_write (create_drawing also through ea_drawing_export). Claim to check: an invalid outline is refused with field paths before any container runs; a revision is a new DocumentVersion of the same generated document in the caller's organization, and another organization's document is not found. BI-84C1F526 (DI-4B843FAF62F9) adds issue_grok_credentials_client to the existing surface-readiness pack. Grok's credential is a client_credentials OAuth client that only a container script could create, so an agent on a consumer host had no way to converge it. The tool reuses ensureGrokCredentialsClient: one client per owner, no personal access token, no new token kind. Claim to check: it returns the caller's own client, refuses a caller narrower than dpf.read dpf.work dpf.build, and its secret never reaches the audit row. Outside the core tier. EP-07B49BD8 (BI-9CD95438, BI-07F52DA6): resume_workroom_queue releases a Workroom held after a provider failure; no existing tool clears drive state, and update_workroom_status overrides status, not the hold. drive_workroom_runtime is the single entry point for a room's supervised agent-CLI session (start, turn, steer, interrupt, stop, decide, status as one action enum rather than seven tools). approve_runtime_permission is the fixed-name tool Claude Code's --permission-prompt-tool must call; it answers only a room session credential. Claim to check: a held room dispatches nothing until resumed; a room session credential is refused for any other room and revoked when the session stops; an outward CLI action is held for a room decision, never bypassed. BI-129EFFD1 adds probe_pending_approval_conversion to the existing coworker pack: the AC-PROBE dry run of every pending proposal, run inside the server on read-only transactions so an admin or the coordinating session can record it as evidence without host database credentials. It replaces no tool; the local script now calls the same runner. BI-1914A351: get_provider_accounts and manage_provider_account provide scoped account controls; their independent-account claim remains. BI-CAP-1774FB7A adds review_workroom_sensitivity and correct_workroom_sensitivity in the existing Workroom pack. The admin reader returns only a revision digest and known/unknown classification state because get_workroom correctly refuses protected contents. The separate authority-consequential writer requires administrator classification review, exact digest and rationale, and retains the original declaration in an audit. Ordinary boundary edits cannot safely repair historical unknown labels. Claim to check: denied-room information is never returned, valid labels cannot be downgraded through recovery, stale corrections are refused and original records remain. Both tools stay outside the core tier; no tool per classification or global clearance control. BI-CAP-E7AE57C2 adds verify_archetype_projection: the missing no-argument DEV/test-only live lifecycle check, which uses production reconciliation and rolls back its own fixture. Existing setup/reset targets business content; source tests cannot verify the served image. Claim to check: stable identity, withdrawal/restoration, retained references and history without durable fixture writes or selecting existing organizations. BI-5ACBAC50: preview_runtime_capability_reconciliation establishes validated read-only host/database baselines; reconcile_runtime_capabilities applies explicit intent through the existing signed ledger with manage_platform/admin_write and platform-authority consequence. Separate names make read versus mutation authority legible. Claim to check: preview never selects or activates settings; apply preserves authenticated actor, immutable packet, untouched state and later-writer refusal. Both remain in the existing platform-update pack; no extra core-tier entry or live grant expansion. BI-0ACB97B5 adds get_investment_balance, set_investment_balance and bind_investment_funding in the existing portfolio-budget pack. They expose one scoped read, one revisioned owner policy write and one explicit room/portfolio/install funding binding across portal and external agents; points-budget tools cannot express token allocation or funding provenance. Claim to check: matching portal/MCP authority, stale revision refusal, no administrator-derived ownership, cross-organization isolation and immutable attempt attribution. No new pack or core-tier names. BI-10AC904B / DI-1F9835170DA5 adds issue_source_credentials_client to the existing surface-readiness pack: the Grok issuer has a different purpose, and the manual form requires an operator handoff. This caller-bound entry point reuses the owned-client mechanism with fixed scopes, authenticated owner and assistant binding, serialized idempotence and secret-result redaction. It accepts no arbitrary recipient or scope, expands no grant and adds no core-tier name. Claim to check: an eligible caller obtains only its own source client; ambiguity, foreign ownership, missing authority and unreadable secrets refuse without replacement. BI-63FB1683 Phase E adds broadcast_workroom_ask and acknowledge_workroom_broadcast on the existing room-messaging pack. COO asks fan contains descendants through post_room_message plus a WorkroomActivity ask/ack ledger; no existing tool fans out or records acknowledgements. They stay off the core tier, grant work_room_write, and never dispatch a stage. Claim to check: dispatchInvoked is always false; missing acknowledgements are reported; a derived owner is never a stall recipient.

registry.packFiles.reason: BI-012487AA: document-family-tools.ts holds the four render-family tool definitions and their one shared handler, composed into the existing document pack (the provider-account-tools.ts pattern), so document-pack.ts does not grow toward the module ceiling. Not a second registration path: document-pack.test.ts proves each tool is registered once with grants equal to the single source in document-tool-grants.ts. BI-1914A351: provider-account-tools.ts holds the two account tool definitions composed into the existing model-provider pack. Handlers remain in that pack and delegate to shared account services, avoiding a larger import cycle. This is an account contract module, not a second tool registration path. Claim to check: model-provider pack tests prove one registration and matching grants for each account control. BI-B8437D03 extracts the existing five nonproduction lease definitions into nonprod-lease-definitions.ts, composed once by the existing nonprod-lease pack. This keeps timing validation and handlers below the module ceiling without adding a tool, core-tier entry, grant or registration path. Claim to check: existing pack tests retain the same five names, grants and handlers, with requestedTtlMs constrained to an integer; tool-definition and dispatch baselines remain unchanged.

tier.coreToolNames.reason: Adds the five names without which a core-tier client can start governed work but never finish it: update_backlog_item_status and record_execution_evidence (AGENTS.md s5 requires recording completion and its evidence, and core could create/triage/size/update but not close); trace_code_surface (a surface's implementation files and tests, pairing with search_code_graph which is already core); and claim_nonprod_environment_lease with release_nonprod_environment_lease together, since a session that can take the shared singleton lock but not release it blocks every other worktree and the CI gate. A client that cannot close its own work reaches for ?tier=full and pays the whole ~400-tool surface to recover two names. No effect on Claude Code or Codex, whose client-aware default is already full. Raise again only for a tool without which governed work cannot be finished; convenience stays behind search_tool_marketplace.
